prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Scope: checked baggage from acceptance (bag-drop/transfer induction) through screening, sorting, make-up, to outbound load control handoff. Elements: Pier 4 Bag-Drop Unit (records accepted bag; sends Oversize Exception Ticket); Bag Tag Printer (tag with unique ID; produces Calibration Witness Tag when calibration witness record required); Transfer Bag Feeder (records transfer bags; sends Late Transfer Bag Card; holds bags until screening status/onward handling confirmed); Induction Tray Conveyor (controlled spacing for image capture and identification before route selection); Baggage Control System, alias Velvet (associates tag with passenger/flight record; checks flight open/record complete; validates transfer routing; applies screening profile; loads approved sort plan with effective time window before sortation; checks plan against flight/handling records before assigning route; routes exception bags to Secondary Inspection Chute); Concourse Zone Controller, alias Mosslight (induction permissive; Recovery Route Card; coordinates conveyor availability with sort plan); Flight Data Gateway, alias Lantern (flight/routing records; Flight Cutoff Advisory); Primary Crossbelt Sorter, alias Juniper (maintains identity, applies assigned destination and screening status; sends Chute Occupancy Note when lane nears limit); North Gate Scanner, alias Kestrel, and South Gate Scanner (Manual Rescan Receipt): read/verify bag ID at route decision points, acquire images, return disposition, record image quality/alarm; Image Resolution Desk (staff record disposition); Secondary Inspection Chute (occupancy monitored; authorized-access only); Bag Reconciliation Station (verifies bag matches screening record); East/West Make-Up Conveyor; Carousel 7 Make-Up Unit, alias Orchard (accepts only valid disposition + authorized routing); Outbound Load Control Desk. Actors: Baggage Operations Supervisor (flight readiness, staffing, lane decisions; notified on isolation); Explosives Response Team, alias Pebble (escalated alarms, coordinates safety with airport security); Security Duty Manager (notified for non-routine security decisions); Maintenance Technician; Airline Ramp Coordinator (Carousel Release Slip); inspection staff. States: clear, exception, awaiting review. Requirements: hold missing/conflicting-data and oversized bags until route confirmed; induction needs valid record, route, ready equipment; interlocks stop feed on jam/door/downstream loss; incomplete exam never clear; awaiting-review barred from make-up; clear routes normally only if identity and record agree; alarm/unresolved → exception; no release into blocked chute; alarmed bag kept under staff control until authorized

New part:
S088: A scan mismatch prevents the bag from continuing on a route that depends on the unresolved identity.
S089: Congestion awareness uses current lane availability, conveyor stops, and the observed rate of incoming bags.
S090: The Baggage Operations Supervisor sets local congestion thresholds and confirms the authorized response to sustained overload.
S091: Tern is the operational alias used for the Baggage Operations Supervisor in sortation coordination.
S092: When a planned lane is unavailable, the Baggage Control System selects an approved alternate route only if screening status and flight timing remain valid.
S093: Bags with an unresolved destination or a route outside their handling limits are diverted to the Secondary Inspection Chute.
S094: The Image Resolution Desk resolves image-related holds before affected bags are returned to normal sortation.
S095: The Explosives Response Team manages security holds under the applicable response procedures.
S096: A bag returns to normal handling only after its identity, examination outcome, and routing authorization agree.
S097: The East Make-Up Conveyor and West Make-Up Conveyor are selected according to the active plan and available capacity.
S098: The Carousel 7 Make-Up Unit operates within its assigned flight window and reports when its usable capacity is constrained.
S099: The Transfer Bag Feeder continues to hold transfer bags until screening status and intended onward handling are confirmed.
S100: The Bag Reconciliation Station compares bag identity with the active handling record and flags unresolved discrepancies.
S101: The Bag Reconciliation Station sends a Bag Match Query when bag identity cannot be reconciled with the active handling record.
S102: Bags found on a stopped or misdirected path are held from onward movement until their location and identity are established.
S103: The Maintenance Technician isolates a failed conveyor section and confirms that the route is safe before service resumes.
S104: The Baggage Operations Supervisor authorizes recovery to the approved sort plan after the cause of the abnormal path has been addressed.
S105: Flight Data Gateway maintains scheduled flight identifiers, destinations, planned departure times, and revisions needed for baggage planning.
S106: Flight schedules include airline-specific dispatch targets and connection windows, and changes are time-stamped for operational use.
S107: Baggage Control System evaluates flight assignments against current schedule data before accepting bag routing instructions.
S108: The planned dispatch time is the reference for prioritizing bags, while the published departure time remains the passenger-facing schedule value.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
